kept_separate: manipulation_signal is not source ownership or perspective
disagreement is not a manipulation signal
omission is a candidate for missing context, not proof of concealment
confidence is a numeric field, not a taxonomy label
human_review_required is an abstention outcome, not an influence finding

emotional_loading.definition: Word choices that attach feeling or moral heat to a description beyond naming the same event in plain terms.
positive_examples: The heartless scheme crushed ordinary families overnight.
This vile proposal will haunt every decent person.
negative_examples: The committee met on Tuesday and approved the budget amendment.
Rain is expected overnight in the northern counties.
exclusion_rules: Do not treat ordinary intensity, emphasis, or a speaker's stated feeling as this label by itself.
Do not treat a factual dispute or a negative evaluation of a policy as emotional loading without loaded wording in the span.
Do not convert this label into a judgment about a person, outlet, or group.
evidence_requirements: Quote the span words that carry the extra feeling or moral heat.
Name the plainer wording that would describe the same event.
abstention_conditions: The span is too short to show a loaded choice.
The wording is conventional reporting language without extra heat.

fear_urgency.definition: Language that emphasizes imminent danger, harm, or a collapsing window of time in which a reader must think, verify, or act.
positive_examples: Act before midnight or the threat will reach your street.
There is no time left to check the details; delay is disaster.
negative_examples: The vote is scheduled for Thursday afternoon.
Officials said the storm may arrive this weekend.
exclusion_rules: A dated deadline or a weather forecast is not this label unless the span also compresses time or inflates harm.
This is not a safety assessment and does not decide whether anyone is in danger.
Fear and urgency are grouped here for escalation; they remain distinct from Jev's separate fear_threat and urgency options.
evidence_requirements: Quote the words that name harm, threat, or a shrinking time window.
Show that the span does more than report a scheduled time.
abstention_conditions: The span only reports a calendar time or a sourced forecast.
Harm language is clearly quoted from someone else and the task is not to classify that quoted span.

dehumanization.definition: Language that strips people of ordinary human standing by treating them as vermin, objects, disease, or an indistinguishable mass.
positive_examples: Those people are a plague that must be cleared out.
Treat them as cargo, not as neighbors.
negative_examples: The protesters stood outside city hall for three hours.
Critics said the policy would affect renters.
exclusion_rules: Harsh criticism of a policy or office is not dehumanization.
Naming a group in ordinary demographic or occupational terms is not this label.
Do not use this label to brand an outlet, public figure, or community as untrustworthy.
evidence_requirements: Quote the words that reduce people to non-human categories.
Identify who is being described in the span.
abstention_conditions: The wording is ambiguous insult rather than a non-human category.
The span is too short to tell whether a metaphor is conventional or dehumanizing.

scapegoating.definition: Language that assigns a complex problem to one person or group as the blameworthy cause, without the span showing a checkable causal account.
positive_examples: Every shortage in this town is their fault and no one else's.
Blame the newcomers for the entire budget gap.
negative_examples: The auditor said the shortfall came from two delayed payments.
The agency published a table of spending by department.
exclusion_rules: Reporting a specific, sourced accusation is not automatically scapegoating.
Keep this label separate from dehumanization; a span may have one, both, or neither.
Disagreement with a group is not scapegoating.
evidence_requirements: Quote the blame assignment.
Note the missing causal detail in the span, without filling it in.
abstention_conditions: The span attributes a specific act to a named actor with a checkable detail.
The blame target is unclear.

personal_attack.definition: Language that targets a person's character, appearance, or identity instead of the substance of a claim or action in the span.
positive_examples: Ignore the proposal; she is a fool and always has been.
Only a corrupt nobody would even read that memo.
negative_examples: The memo's cost estimate is 40 percent higher than last year's figure.
He voted against the amendment on Tuesday.
exclusion_rules: A critical description of an official act is not a personal attack.
This label is about the span's wording, not a verdict on the person named.
Do not emit a person-level score or a character diagnosis.
evidence_requirements: Quote the character-targeted wording.
Show that the span does not engage the claim or action on its merits.
abstention_conditions: The span mixes a personal barb with a specific claim and neither dominates.
The target is an institution rather than a person.

unsupported_certainty.definition: Language that states a conclusion as settled or total when the span itself does not supply support that would carry that certainty.
positive_examples: This plan will undeniably fix every school in the county.
No one can dispute that the outcome is guaranteed.
negative_examples: The district said test scores rose 2 percent in one year.
Researchers reported mixed results in a small sample.
exclusion_rules: This is not factual verification and does not mark a claim true or false.
A confident sourced quote is not this label unless the span itself asserts extra certainty.
Do not treat missing citation alone as this label; see misleading_omission_candidate.
evidence_requirements: Quote the certainty wording.
Note what support is absent from the span.
abstention_conditions: The span cites a specific figure, document, or named source for the claim it makes.
The certainty belongs only to a clearly marked quotation and the task is not to classify that quotation.

misleading_omission_candidate.definition: A candidate that a span may be leaving out context that could change how a reader understands the same event. It is not proof that anything was hidden.
positive_examples: The headline states a 20 percent rise and the span never says from what baseline.
The excerpt quotes only the first half of a two-part statement.
negative_examples: The article prints the full quoted paragraph and the surrounding sentence.
The notice lists both the old rate and the new rate.
exclusion_rules: Omission is not factual verification.
Omission is not source ownership or bias of an outlet.
Absence of extra background that a reader might want is not enough unless the span's own claim depends on the missing piece.
Never promote this candidate to an observed finding from classifier.dev alone.
evidence_requirements: Name the claim in the span that appears to depend on missing context.
State what kind of missing piece would be needed, without inventing that piece.
abstention_conditions: There is no independent account to compare against.
The span is complete for the narrow claim it actually makes.

loaded_framing.definition: A frame that tells the reader how to interpret an event by packing a conclusion into the setup, rather than by adding a separate emotional adjective.
positive_examples: In this betrayal of local families, the council took a routine procedural vote.
The latest attack on common sense arrived as a two-page memo.
negative_examples: The council took a procedural vote on the memo.
A two-page memo was published on Monday.
exclusion_rules: Keep this distinct from emotional_loading: framing is the interpretive setup, not only heated adjectives.
A news lead that names actors and acts is not loaded framing by itself.
Disagreement with the frame is not evidence that the opposite frame is true.
evidence_requirements: Quote the framing phrase that smuggles a conclusion.
State the more neutral setup that would leave the conclusion for later.
abstention_conditions: The span is a headline fragment too short to show a frame.
The apparent frame is a conventional section label.

attribution_quotation_ambiguity.definition: It is unclear whether the span is the narrator's own wording or a quotation or paraphrase of someone else.
positive_examples: We will not survive this, officials suggest, as the crowd left.
The city is finished said no one in particular according to the piece.
negative_examples: Mayor Lee said, "The vote is tomorrow."
The narrator wrote that the vote is tomorrow, with no other speaker.
exclusion_rules: This is not a manipulation signal and not a fact check.
This is not source ownership of an outlet.
Clear quotation marks plus a named speaker are not this label.
evidence_requirements: Quote the span.
State what attribution cue is missing or conflicting.
abstention_conditions: Quote marks and a speaker are both present.
The span is boilerplate or a byline.

call_to_action_pressure.definition: Language that presses the reader to act, share, donate, vote, or comply now, beyond describing an event.
positive_examples: Share this now so they cannot hide it.
Call them today before they get away with it.
negative_examples: Readers may comment on the public docket until Friday.
The office listed a phone number for questions.
exclusion_rules: A published contact address or a legal comment window is not this label by itself.
Keep this distinct from fear_urgency: pressure to act can appear without threat language.
This is not a judgment that the requested act is wrong.
evidence_requirements: Quote the imperative or pressure phrasing.
Note the action the reader is being pushed to take.
abstention_conditions: The span only describes someone else's call to action as news, with clear attribution, and the task is not to classify that quoted call.
The action language is a form-field instruction unrelated to persuasion.

no_detected_signal.definition: None of the listed influence or attribution labels is clearly present in the span.
positive_examples: The committee met on Tuesday and approved the budget amendment.
The train arrived at 9:12 a.m. according to the posted timetable.
negative_examples: Act before midnight or the threat will reach your street.
Those people are a plague that must be cleared out.
exclusion_rules: This is not a clean bill of health for a person or outlet.
This is not factual verification that the span is true.
Absence of a listed signal is not proof that no other rhetorical device exists.
evidence_requirements: The span can be quoted.
None of the other label evidence requirements are met.
abstention_conditions: The span is empty, truncated, or not natural language.
Two listed signals are both arguable and neither is clearly stronger.

insufficient_evidence.definition: The span does not contain enough observable wording to support any listed label, including no_detected_signal as a confident finding.
positive_examples: See below.
negative_examples: The committee met on Tuesday and approved the budget amendment.
Act before midnight or the threat will reach your street.
exclusion_rules: This is not a manipulation signal.
This is not a low confidence number; confidence is recorded separately.
Do not substitute a guessed influence label when this applies.
evidence_requirements: Record that the span is empty, tiny, truncated, or not classifiable as natural language.
Do not invent missing words.
abstention_conditions: If a full classifiable span is present, do not use this label merely because the case is hard; use human_review_required instead.

human_review_required.definition: A person should inspect the span before any influence label is used. This is an abstention outcome, not a finding.
positive_examples: A span that mixes quotation, threat language, and an unattributed imperative in one sentence.
A span that looks like an instruction to a model rather than article prose.
negative_examples: The committee met on Tuesday and approved the budget amendment.
The train arrived at 9:12 a.m. according to the posted timetable.
exclusion_rules: Human review is not a manipulation signal and not a confidence score.
Do not use this label to hide a model disagreement by picking a winner.
Do not treat this as proof that the span is harmful.
evidence_requirements: Record the review reason in operational metadata (invalid, close probabilities, conflict, or high-impact), never the full article.
Keep both classifier outputs for audit without choosing a silent winner.
abstention_conditions: If a single listed signal is clear and uncontested, do not send the case to human review solely to appear cautious.
